classification.difficultyReason: Calibrate the supplied squared-period/cubed-distance model, retain the unrounded constant, recover a positive period and convert units, then interpret the physical assumptions limiting the model. The algebra is guided; identifying contextual limitations is the hardest demand.

content.prompt: In astrophysics, the orbital period $T$ of a planet around a star is related to the length of the semi-major axis, $a$, of its orbit via Kepler’s third law: roughly $T^2=ka^3$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If Earth has a semi-major axis of 2609 astronomical units (AU) and an orbital period of 365 days, find the constant of proportionality. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the orbital period for Saturn which has a semi-major axis of 24 900 AU. Give the period in days to the nearest 10 days, and in years to 1 decimal place. Use 365 days per year.

answer.short:
10 760 days, or 29.5 years, using the printed data.

Use the unrounded constant from part (a).
answer.worked:
Using the exact constant from part (a) and taking the positive square root:
$$\begin{align*}T&=\sqrt{\frac{365^2}{2609^3}\times24900^3}\\T&=365\left(\frac{24900}{2609}\right)^{3/2}\\T&\approx10760\text{ days}\end{align*}$$
Using the unrounded period:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Period in years}&=\left(\frac{24900}{2609}\right)^{3/2}\\\text{Period in years}&\approx29.5\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Discuss any limitations of this model.

answer.short: It assumes motion around one dominant star and neglects other gravitational influences. The constant depends on the star, and the orbit must avoid the star.
answer.worked: The model applies approximately when the star dominates the gravitational interaction. A different star generally requires a different constant. Other bodies can disturb the orbit, especially where their gravitational influence becomes significant. Very small orbits must avoid intersecting the star; weaker gravity alone does not mean that a distant orbit must stop.
